source.title: NEXUS-O: An Omni-Perceptive and -Interactive Model for Language, Audio, and Vision
source.authors: Che Liu; Yingji Zhang; Dong Zhang; Wei-Jie Zhang; Chenggong Gong; Haohan Li; Yu Lu; Shilin Zhou; Yue Lu; Zi-Liang Gan; Ziao Wang; Junwei Liao; Haipang Wu; Ji Liu; Andr'e Freitas; Qi-Fan Wang; Zeng-Lin Xu; Rongjunchen Zhang; Yong Dai

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures vision-language representation alignment with several kernel-alignment metrics and reports different comparative outcomes across metrics, bearing on metric dependence (V6). It does not test scale-dependent convergence between independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The representation-alignment analyses in Table 7 are relevant to V6. The paper does not test whether alignment rises with scale or capability, convergence across seeds, or whether representations are interchangeable. The downstream task benchmark results do not measure the claim versions. Table 7 reports scores for each model and metric separately; Figure 3 is described as showing higher alignment with audio at most hidden layers.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the Platonic-hypothesis kernel-alignment metrics (cka, cknna, svcca, knn variants) to score vision-language alignment inside single multimodal LLMs. It uses them to show that its own model, NEXUS-O, with or without audio, beats its backbone and other MLLMs. It never tests whether independently trained models converge with scale or capability (V1/V2). It does not examine seeds (V3), maps (V4) or shared features (V5). It does not argue or test metric or data dependence of convergence (V6): differing outcomes across metrics are reported only as win counts for its own model. It does not address the extent or causes of convergence (V7). This is the study's own method compared with baselines, so it does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, with one correction. The authors claim audio incorporation enhances vision-language alignment: on Table 7, NEXUS-O beats its backbone on 5 of 7 metrics without audio, and with audio it leads on 4 of 7. For Figure 3 they say audio significantly enhances alignment, especially in intermediate layers. They present this as evidence that their training strategy works, not as a finding about convergence. Their abstract states the audio-enhancement claim without the metric caveat.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates cross-modal representation alignment using CKA, CKNNA, SVCCA, and four KNN-based metrics; it is not a scale sweep or an explicit replication of the original convergence claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported comparative results vary across the seven alignment metrics. Figure 3 also examines hidden layers and reports improved alignment with audio at most layers; the text gives no layerwise numerical values.

fits_no_version.finding: Within NEXUS-O, adding audio (TTS audio concatenated with vision embeddings, or fed jointly) raises vision-language kernel alignment. This holds on 4 of 7 metrics on ImageNet concepts and at most hidden layers on WIT, per the authors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a multimodal LLM, adding a third modality aligned with language increases vision-language representational alignment.

record.problems: The alignment analysis uses one stated dataset per stage (ImageNet concepts for Table 7 and Wikipedia-caption corpus for Figure 3); no uncertainty estimates are reported. Figure 3's results are shown only as a plot. No scale or capability comparison is conducted.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from Table 7 or Figure 3. Other task benchmark results were excluded because they do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no comparison of independently trained models.
Alignment is measured within jointly trained MLLMs, not between separate vision and language models. No test of alignment rising with model quality.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability tests.
No shared interpretable features or circuits.
No designed test of metric, neighbour-count or input dependence of convergence. Metric disagreement appears only incidentally in own-model win counts.
No analysis of plateau, incompleteness or causes of convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. Mixed win counts for the authors' own model are not a test of metric dependence of convergence, and the authors never frame them that way. Incidentally, Table 7 rankings disagree sharply across metrics: Phi3.5 scores 0.028 on cycle knn but is near the top on cka (0.086). Someone could reuse this as raw data on metric disagreement, but the paper draws no such conclusion. The metrics come from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis paper (ref 34), which is used only as a tool. Single dataset per stage, no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep and no test of convergence between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
The paper measures image-language alignment, but does not test whether alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison across random seeds or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
The paper compares several metrics on its reported data, but does not test metric settings such as neighbour count, out-of-distribution inputs, or whether alignment vanishes under those choices.
No test of a plateau, incomplete convergence between independently trained models, or shared-training-data/objective explanations.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Table 7 metric comparisons on ImageNet concepts
reader_labels.reason: Alignment comparisons differ across the seven metrics: NEXUS-O without audio is reported better than its backbone on 5 of 7 metrics, while vision+audio outperforms others on 4 of 7; see T7-N-cyc through T7-NA-edit.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layerwise embedding-stage analysis on the Wikipedia-caption corpus
reader_labels.reason: The paper describes an audio-associated alignment improvement at most hidden layers, not all layers; Figure 3 provides no numerical values in the text (F3-OA).
